help.aligndrill:
Create an Excellon object with drills for alignment.
> aligndrill name [-dia <float>] [-box <str>] [-holes <str>] [-grid <float>] [-gridoffset <float>] [-minoffset <float>] [-axisoffset <float>] -axis <str> [-dist <float>] [-outname <str>]
	name <str>: Name of the object (Gerber or Excellon) to mirror.
	[-dia <float>: Tool diameter]
	[-box <str>: Name of object which act as box (cutout for example.)]
	[-holes <str>: Tuple of tuples where each tuple it is a set of x, y coordinates. E.g: (x0, y0), (x1, y1), ... ]
	[-grid <float>: Aligning to grid, for those, who have aligning pinsinside table in grid (-5,0),(5,0),(15,0)...]
	[-gridoffset <float>: offset of grid from 0 position.]
	[-minoffset <float>: min and max distance between align hole and pcb.]
	[-axisoffset <float>: Offset on second axis before aligment holes]
	-axis <str>: Mirror axis parallel to the X or Y axis.
	[-dist <float>: Distance of the mirror axis to the X or Y axis.]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Excellon object.]
	[-timeout <int>: Max wait for job timeout before error.]
> aligndrill my_object -axis X -box my_object -dia 3.125 -grid 1 -gridoffset 0 -minoffset 2 -axisoffset 2

	-gridy <float>: Grid size in Y axis.

help.cncjob:
Generates a CNC Job object from a Geometry Object.
> cncjob [name] [-dia <float>] [-z_cut <float>] [-z_move <float>] [-feedrate <float>] [-feedrate_z <float>] [-feedrate_rapid <float>] [-extracut_length <float>] [-dpp <float>] [-toolchangez <float>] [-toolchangexy <str>] [-startz <float>] [-endz <float>] [-endxy <str>] [-spindlespeed <int>] [-dwelltime <float>] [-outname <str>] [-pp <str>] [-muted <str>]
	[name <str>: Name of the source object.]
	[-dia <float>: Tool diameter to show on screen.]
	[-z_cut <float>: Z-axis cutting position.]
	[-z_move <float>: Z-axis moving position.]
	[-feedrate <float>: Moving speed on X-Y plane when cutting.]
	[-feedrate_z <float>: Moving speed on Z plane when cutting.]
	[-feedrate_rapid <float>: Rapid moving at speed when cutting.]
	[-extracut_length <float>: The value for extra cnccut over the first point in path,in the job end; float]
	[-dpp <float>: If present then use multidepth cnc cut. Height of one layer for multidepth.]
	[-toolchangez <float>: Z distance for toolchange (example: 30.0).
If used in the command then a toolchange event will be included in gcode]
	[-toolchangexy <str>: The X,Y coordinates at Toolchange event in format (x, y) (example: (30.0, 15.2) or without parenthesis like: 0.3,1.0). WARNING: no spaces allowed in the value.]
	[-startz <float>: Height before the first move.]
	[-endz <float>: Height where the last move will park.]
	[-endxy <str>: The X,Y coordinates at job end in format (x, y) (example: (2.0, 1.2) or without parenthesislike: 0.3,1.0). WARNING: no spaces allowed in the value.]
	[-spindlespeed <int>: Speed of the spindle in rpm (example: 4000).]
	[-dwelltime <float>: Time to pause to allow the spindle to reach the full speed.
If it is not used in command then it will not be included]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Geometry object.]
	[-pp <str>: Name of the Geometry preprocessor. No quotes, case sensitive]
	[-muted <str>: It will not put errors in the Shell. Can be True (1) or False (0)]
	[-timeout <int>: Max wait for job timeout before error.]
> cncjob geo_name -dia 0.5 -z_cut -1.7 -z_move 2 -feedrate 120 -pp default
help.ncc_clear:
Clear excess copper in polygons. Basically it's a negative Paint.
> ncc_clear name [-tooldia <str>] [-overlap <float>] [-margin <float>] [-order <str>] [-method <str>] [-connect <str>] [-contour <str>] [-rest <str>] [-offset <float>] [-all <int>] [-box <str>] [-outname <str>]
> ncc name [-tooldia <str>] [-overlap <float>] [-margin <float>] [-order <str>] [-method <str>] [-connect <str>] [-contour <str>] [-rest <str>] [-offset <float>] [-all <int>] [-box <str>] [-outname <str>]
	name <str>: Name of the source Geometry object. String.
	[-tooldia <str>: Diameter of the tool to be used. Can be a comma separated list of diameters.
WARNING: No space is allowed between tool diameters. E.g: correct: 0.5,1 / incorrect: 0.5, 1]
	[-overlap <float>: Percentage of tool diameter to overlap current pass over previous pass. Float [0, 99.9999]
E.g: for a 25% from tool diameter overlap use -overlap 25]
	[-margin <float>: Bounding box margin. Float number.]
	[-order <str>: Can have the values: "no", "fwd" and "rev". String.It is useful when there are multiple tools in tooldia parameter."no" -> the order used is the one provided."fwd" -> tools are ordered from smallest to biggest."rev" -> tools are ordered from biggest to smallest.]
	[-method <str>: Algorithm for copper clearing. Can be: "standard", "seed" or "lines".]
	[-connect <str>: Draw lines to minimize tool lifts. True (1) or False (0)]
	[-contour <str>: Cut around the perimeter of the painting. True (1) or False (0)]
	[-rest <str>: Use rest-machining. True (1) or False (0)]
	[-offset <float>: If used, the copper clearing will finish to a distance from copper features. Float number.]
	[-all <int>: If used will copper clear the whole object. Either "-all" or "-box <value>" has to be used.]
	[-box <str>: Name of the object to be used as reference. Either "-all" or "-box <value>" has to be used. String.]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Geometry object. String. No spaces.]
> ncc obj_name -tooldia 0.3,1 -overlap 10 -margin 1.0 -method 'lines' -all

help.drillcncjob:
Generates a Drill CNC Job from a Excellon Object.
> drillcncjob name [-drilled_dias <str>] [-drillz <float>] [-dpp <float>] [-travelz <float>] [-feedrate_z <float>] [-feedrate_rapid <float>] [-spindlespeed <int>] [-toolchangez <float>] [-toolchangexy <str>] [-startz <float>] [-endz <float>] [-endxy <str>] [-dwelltime <float>] [-pp <str>] [-opt_type <str>] [-diatol <float>] [-muted <str>] [-outname <str>]
	name <str>: Name of the source object.
	[-drilled_dias <str>: Comma separated tool diameters of the drills to be drilled (example: 0.6,1.0 or 3.125). WARNING: No space allowed]
	[-drillz <float>: Drill depth into material (example: -2.0). Negative value.]
	[-dpp <float>: Progressive drilling into material with a specified step (example: 0.7). Positive value.]
	[-travelz <float>: Travel distance above material (example: 2.0).]
	[-feedrate_z <float>: Drilling feed rate. It is the speed on the Z axis.]
	[-feedrate_rapid <float>: Rapid drilling feed rate.]
	[-spindlespeed <int>: Speed of the spindle in rpm (example: 4000).]
	[-toolchangez <float>: Z distance for toolchange (example: 30.0).
If used in the command then a toolchange event will be included in gcode]
	[-toolchangexy <str>: The X,Y coordinates at Toolchange event in format (x, y) (example: (30.0, 15.2) or without parenthesis like: 0.3,1.0). WARNING: no spaces allowed in the value.]
	[-startz <float>: The Z coordinate at job start (example: 30.0).]
	[-endz <float>: The Z coordinate at job end (example: 30.0).]
	[-endxy <str>: The X,Y coordinates at job end in format (x, y) (example: (2.0, 1.2) or without parenthesislike: 0.3,1.0). WARNING: no spaces allowed in the value.]
	[-dwelltime <float>: Time to pause to allow the spindle to reach the full speed.
If it is not used in command then it will not be included]
	[-pp <str>: This is the Excellon preprocessor name: case_sensitive, no_quotes]
	[-opt_type <str>: Name of move optimization type. B by default for Basic OR-Tools, M for Metaheuristic OR-ToolsT from Travelling Salesman Algorithm. B and M works only for 64bit version of FlatCAM and T works only for 32bit version of FlatCAM]
	[-diatol <float>: Tolerance. Percentange (0.0 ... 100.0) within which dias in drilled_dias will be judged to be the same as the ones in the tools from the Excellon object. E.g: if in drill_dias we have a diameter with value 1.0, in the Excellon we have a tool with dia = 1.05 and we set a tolerance diatol = 5.0 then the drills with the dia = (0.95 ... 1.05) in Excellon will be processed. Float number.]
	[-muted <str>: It will not put errors in the Shell or status bar. Can be True (1) or False (0).]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Geometry object.]
	[-timeout <int>: Max wait for job timeout before error.]
> drillcncjob test.TXT -drillz -1.5 -travelz 14 -feedrate_z 222 -feedrate_rapid 456 -spindlespeed 777 -toolchangez 33 -endz 22 -pp default
Usage of -feedrate_rapid matter only when the preprocessor is using it, like -marlin-.
> drillcncjob test.DRL -drillz -1.7 -dpp 0.5 -travelz 2 -feedrate_z 800 -endxy 3,3

> isolate name [-dia <float>] [-passes <int>] [-overlap <float>] [-combine <str>] [-outname <str>] [-follow <str>] [-iso_type <int>]
	name <str>: Name of the Gerber source object to be isolated. Required.
	[-dia <float>: Tool diameter.]
	[-passes <int>: Passes of tool width.]
	[-overlap <float>: Percentage of tool diameter to overlap current pass over previous pass. Float [0, 99.9999]
E.g: for a 25% from tool diameter overlap use -overlap 25]
	[-combine <str>: Combine all passes into one geometry. Can be True (1) or False (0)]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Geometry object.]
	[-follow <str>: Create a Geometry that follows the Gerber path. Can be True (1) or False (0).]
	[-iso_type <int>: A value of 0 will isolate exteriors, a value of 1 will isolate interiors and a value of 2 will do full isolation.]
	[-timeout <int>: Max wait for job timeout before error.]
> isolate my_gerber -dia 0.1 -passes 2 -overlap 10 -combine True -iso_type 2 -outname out_geo

help.milldrills:
Create a Geometry Object for milling drill holes from Excellon.
> milldrills name [-milled_dias <str>] [-tooldia <float>] [-outname <str>] [-use_thread <str>] [-diatol <float>]
> milld name [-milled_dias <str>] [-tooldia <float>] [-outname <str>] [-use_thread <str>] [-diatol <float>]
	name <str>: Name of the Excellon Object. Required.
	[-milled_dias <str>: Comma separated tool diameters of the drills to be milled (example: 0.6, 1.0 or 3.125).
Exception: if you enter "all" then the drills for all tools will be milled.
WARNING: no spaces are allowed in the list of tools.
As a precaution you can enclose them with quotes.]
	[-tooldia <float>: Diameter of the milling tool (example: 0.1).]
	[-outname <str>: Name of Geometry object to be created holding the milled geometries.]
	[-use_thread <str>: If to use multithreading: True (1) or False (0).]
	[-diatol <float>: Tolerance. Percentange (0.0 ... 100.0) within which dias in milled_dias will be judged to be the same as the ones in the tools from the Excellon object. E.g: if in milled_dias we have a diameter with value 1.0, in the Excellon we have a tool with dia = 1.05 and we set a tolerance diatol = 5.0 then the drills with the dia = (0.95 ... 1.05) in Excellon will be processed. Float number.]
	[-timeout <int>: Max wait for job timeout before error.]
> milldrills mydrills -milled_dias "0.6,0.8" -tooldia 0.1 -diatol 10 -outname milled_holes
> milld my_excellon.drl

help.paint:
Paint polygons in the specified object by covering them with toolpaths.
Can use only one of the parameters: 'all', 'box', 'single'.
> paint name [-tooldia <str>] [-overlap <float>] [-offset <float>] [-order <str>] [-method <str>] [-connect <str>] [-contour <str>] [-all <str>] [-box <str>] [-single <str>] [-outname <str>]
	name <str>: Name of the source Geometry object. String.
	[-tooldia <str>: Diameter of the tools to be used. Can be a comma separated list of diameters.
WARNING: No space is allowed between tool diameters. E.g: correct: 0.5,1 / incorrect: 0.5, 1]
	[-overlap <float>: Percentage of tool diameter to overlap current pass over previous pass. Float [0, 99.9999]
E.g: for a 25% from tool diameter overlap use -overlap 25]
	[-offset <float>: Distance from the polygon border where painting starts. Float number.]
	[-order <str>: Can have the values: "no", "fwd" and "rev". String.
It is useful when there are multiple tools in tooldia parameter.
"no" -> the order used is the one provided.
"fwd" -> tools are ordered from smallest to biggest.
"rev" -> tools are ordered from biggest to smallest.]
	[-method <str>: Algorithm for painting. Can be: "standard", "seed", "lines", "laser_lines", "combo".]
	[-connect <str>: Draw lines to minimize tool lifts. True (1) or False (0)]
	[-contour <str>: Cut around the perimeter of the painting. True (1) or False (0)]
	[-all <str>: If used, paint all polygons in the object.]
	[-box <str>: name of the object to be used as paint reference. String.]
	[-single <str>: Value is in format x,y or (x,y). Example: 2.0,1.1
If used will paint a single polygon specified by "x" and "y" values.
WARNING: No spaces allowed in the value. Use dot decimals separator.]
	[-outname <str>: Name of the resulting Geometry object. String. No spaces.]
> paint obj_name -tooldia 0.3 -offset 0.1 -method 'seed' -all
> paint obj_name -tooldia 0.3 -offset 0.1 -method 'seed' -single 3.3,2.0

Resizes the object by a factor on X axis and a factor on Y axis, having as scale origin the point
